description:
Finding corrected on 2026-11-13. The `expect_store` substring defect (a server bound to `benchbox-site` accepted `BenchBox-dev/BenchBox`) is already fixed in tractable 1.1.1: `_check_expected_store` in `src/tractable/mcp/resources.py` compares whole trailing path segments, case-insensitively, and `tests/test_mcp_store_report.py::test_check_expected_store_matches_whole_repository_paths` covers the sibling-repository case. BenchBox has vendored 1.1.1 since PR #4144 (2026-11-11), and the global `tractable-mcp` is 1.1.1. No tractable change or release is needed.

What is still wrong:
1. Long-running MCP servers keep the code they started with. A server started on 2026-11-12 08:16 from `_project/scripts/.venv` reports `tool_version` 1.1.0 and still accepted the prefix `BenchBox-dev/Bench` for the store `BenchBox-dev/BenchBox` on 2026-11-13 (the venv was synced to 1.1.1 four minutes after it started). The session that first reported the defect was in the same position. Nothing tells a session that its server is older than the pinned runtime.
2. `.claude/skills/todo/SKILL.md` still says `The match is a case-insensitive substring of the remote only, so pass the full owner/repo`. The skill source lives in the skills catalog, not in this repository.

Expected: the todo skill text states the exact-match rule (changed in the catalog, then `make skill-sync` here), and a session can tell when its tracker server is older than the pinned runtime (for example `get_instructions` or `show_batch` reporting the running version next to the pinned one, or the skill telling agents to compare `capability.tool_version` with the vendored wheel and ask for a restart).

Guardrails: never hand-edit a skill mirror; change the catalog and sync. Do not restart or kill another session's MCP server.
